To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the combination of bibliometric and text mining methods provides a useful tool for mapping the scientific literature; (ii) this combination can be used for research evaluation and information search; (iii) the results are not only useful to the individual researcher, but can also be used to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of the journal Scientometric; and (iv) the methodology can easily be applied to other journals.

(i) full text and bibliographic analysis can be combined in an efficient way to improve the results of both methods, (ii) the results can be used for both information retrieval and research evaluation and (iii) the methodology is not restricted to the analysis of a single document, but can be applied to large sets of papers, as demonstrated by the analysis of 85 Scientometrics papers.

(1) a hybrid method of full text analysis and traditional citation analysis can be applied to research evaluation and information science retrieval; (2) the hybrid approach can be applied to a wide spectrum of bibliometric research, including both theoretical and empirical work; (3) the hybrid method is more effective than either of the two individual approaches; (4) the hybrid approach is more reliable than the full text approach; and (5) the full text approach is more efficient than the citation approach.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question whether a hybrid approach combining full text analysis and traditional citation based bibliometric analysis can be applied for the purpose of mapping scientific disciplines.

the hybrid methodology is applicable to both research evaluation as well as to information retrieval.

the hybrid approach is a promising way to enhance the quality of the results of both information retrieval and research evaluation.
